crucifixion-bramantino
Christ hangs on a cross between mourners in a calm, sharply drawn, cold-colored scene. Bramantino painted it in about 1500, in a style of smooth shapes and clear light.
crucifixion-of-saint-peter

Three men struggle to raise an upside-down cross with Saint Peter nailed to it, who looks at his hands and feet in shock. Caravaggio painted it in 1600, and the light falls on the straining men in the dark.
landscape-with-tobias-and-the-angel
A boy and an angel walk down to a river in a golden, shimmering landscape with trees and distant hills. Claude Lorrain painted it in the 1600s, and the soft glowing light is his trademark.
madonna-with-the-long-neck

Mary sits with a long neck and a huge baby Jesus on her lap, while a row of angels crowds around and a tiny prophet stands in the back. Parmigianino painted it in about 1535, and the stretched, elegant shapes are deliberate.
our-lady-of-the-gate-of-dawn

A gentle icon of Mary with her hands crossed over her chest looks down from a gold and silver frame above a city gate. It was painted around the early 1600s, and in Vilnius, Lithuania, people of many faiths still come to pray before it.
portrait-of-jorge-manuel-theotocopuli
A young man with a pointed beard and a black suit looks out, holding a plan of a building. El Greco painted his son, Jorge Manuel, who was also an artist and an architect, in about 1600.
the-concert-of-the-angels
Angels with lutes, violins and other instruments make a swirling heavenly concert in the clouds. El Greco painted it in about 1600, and the long, flame-like figures are typical of his style.
the-coronation-of-the-virgin
Mary kneels in the clouds as Christ and God the Father place a crown on her head, with angels all around. El Greco painted it in about 1600, and it is a blaze of bright color.
the-martyrdom-of-saint-matthew

An attacker raises his sword over Saint Matthew as he lies on the floor, while people scatter in shock, and an angel hands down a palm branch. Caravaggio painted it in 1600, and he painted himself in the crowd at the back.
amor-vincit-omnia

A cheeky, winged Cupid, grinning, steps on a pile of instruments, armor and books, showing that love wins out over everything. Caravaggio painted it in 1601, and the boy is thought to be a real model.
domine-quo-vadis
Saint Peter, running away from Rome, meets Christ on the road, and falls back in surprise. Annibale Carracci painted it in about 1601, and the legend says Peter turned back to Rome after the meeting.
supper-at-emmaus

Two travelers suddenly recognize the stranger at their dinner table as Christ, and fling out their arms in astonishment. Caravaggio painted it in 1601, and the basket of fruit nearly falls out of the picture.
still-life-with-game-fowl-vegetables-and-fruits

A cabbage, a melon, carrots, a duck and a bird hang and sit against a black background, in a window-like frame. Juan Sánchez Cotán painted it in 1602, and the neat curve of the food is a strange, quiet design.
the-inspiration-of-saint-matthew
An angel hovers over Saint Matthew and guides his hand as he writes the Gospel. Caravaggio painted it in 1602, and the saint looks like a rough working man with dusty feet.
death-of-the-virgin

The apostles weep in a dark room around Mary, who lies on a bed with a swollen body and bare feet, under a big red curtain. Caravaggio painted it in about 1603, and it was rejected by the church that ordered it because it was too real.
the-flight-into-egypt-carracci

Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus travel over a river in a calm, golden landscape, led by a donkey and a guide. Annibale Carracci painted it in 1604, and this tranquil idea of landscape influenced later painters.
david-with-the-head-of-goliath
A young David holds the head of the giant Goliath at arm's length, with a sad look. Caravaggio painted it in about 1605, and the head of Goliath is said to be a self-portrait.
the-beheading-of-saint-john-the-baptist

In a dark prison courtyard, an executioner is about to finish the job while a jailer points and two prisoners watch. Caravaggio painted it in 1608 in Malta, and it is the only painting he ever signed, in the blood.
winter-landscape-with-skaters

A frozen river is crowded with people skating, sledding, playing a game with sticks and fishing in a pale, bright winter day. Hendrick Avercamp painted it in about 1608, and he was deaf and mute and was good at watching people.
fray-hortensio-felix-paravicino
A monk in black with glasses in his hand looks out with a stern, intellectual face. El Greco painted Paravicino, a priest and poet, in about 1609, and it is one of his best portraits.
rubens-and-isabella-brant-in-the-honeysuckle-bower
A young artist and his bride sit on a garden bench under a honeysuckle bush, holding hands and smiling. Peter Paul Rubens painted himself and Isabella Brant in 1609, soon after their wedding.
samson-and-delilah

The strong man Samson lies asleep in the lap of Delilah, while a man cuts off his hair, and soldiers wait at the door. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1609, and Samson's strength comes from his hair.
the-calling-of-saint-matthew

Christ points at a tax collector sitting with friends at a table, and a beam of light falls across the room. Caravaggio painted it in 1599 to 1600, and the question is whether the man points to himself and says, 'Who, me?'
the-flight-into-egypt-elsheimer

Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus walk through a dark forest at night, with a torch, a campfire, the Milky Way and the moon reflected in a pond. Adam Elsheimer painted it in 1609, and it was one of the first pictures to show the stars as they really look.
cobbe-portrait
A man in a gold-edged doublet and a lace collar looks out calmly. Some people think it shows William Shakespeare, painted in about 1610, but it is not sure.
judith-and-her-maidservant

Judith and her maid hurry from the enemy tent carrying a sack with the head of the general, and look back at the sound of someone behind them. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1610, and the light of a candle makes it a thrilling scene.
laocoon
A priest and his sons struggle with giant sea snakes over a stormy view of the city of Toledo. El Greco painted it in about 1610, and the story is told in the Trojan War legend.
merrymakers-at-shrovetide

A group of laughing people sits at a table in costume, with one wearing a fool's hat and another a jester. Frans Hals painted it in about 1615, and the quick brushwork makes them look as if they are laughing right now.
opening-of-the-fifth-seal

Tall, flame-like figures in a stormy sky raise their hands and are given white robes. El Greco painted it in about 1610, and it is a vision from the Book of Revelation, and the picture has been cut at the top.
susanna-and-the-elders
Susanna sits in a bare garden while two old men lean over a wall and whisper to her. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in 1610, when she was just 17, and she shows how upset and trapped Susanna feels.
the-elevation-of-the-cross
A crowd of strong men heaves a huge cross upright in a swirl of muscles and ropes. Peter Paul Rubens painted this triptych in 1610 for a church in Antwerp, where it still hangs.
the-storm-at-sea
Ships toss in a stormy sea, with waves crashing on rocks and the dark sky ripped by lightning. A Flemish painter, thought to be Joos de Momper, painted it in about 1610.
massacre-of-the-innocents

Soldiers on a stage-like street try to take away babies from their mothers, in a very tense moment. Guido Reni painted it in 1611, and it is one of the best examples of a graceful and balanced Italian Baroque painting.
adoration-of-the-shepherds-greco
Shepherds and angels crowd around the glowing newborn Jesus, in long, flame-like shapes under a dark sky. El Greco painted it in about 1612, and he planned it to be hung over his own tomb.
danae-gentilesch
A young woman reclines on her bed as a shower of gold falls onto her, and a maid catches coins in her apron. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1612, and the story is the Greek myth of Danaë.
madonna-and-child-gentilesch

Mary holds the baby Jesus in her arms, dressed in a simple dress with a soft, tender look. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1612, when she was a young painter, and the mother is warmly painted.
the-lute-player
A woman in a golden dress plays the lute, tuning a string, in a warm, gentle scene. Orazio Gentileschi painted this in about 1612 and it is soft and quiet.
judith-slaying-holofernes

Judith and her maid strike down a sleeping general with a sword in a bloody, dramatic scene. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1613, and it is one of her most powerful pictures, with Judith painted as a strong, determined woman.
allegory-of-inclination

A woman sits with a compass, which points at a star above her head, in a bare, glowing room. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1615 for the ceiling of a house in Florence, and she was also an inventor of her own symbols.
allegory-of-the-dutch-victory-over-the-spanish-fleet-at
Dutch ships set fire to Spanish ones in a crowded sea battle, with fire, smoke and splashes. Adam Willaerts painted it in about 1615 to celebrate a Dutch victory at Gibraltar in 1607.
saint-catherine-of-alexandria
A young woman in a red robe leans on the spiked wheel, which was the tool used to torture her, and looks up to heaven. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1619.
self-portrait-as-a-female-martyr
A woman looks up with a palm branch in her hand, a sign of a martyr, in a close, dramatic picture. Artemisia Gentileschi painted herself in about 1615.
self-portrait-with-parents-brothers-and-sisters
A big family gathers to make music and sing, with a dog, a father with a guitar, a mother and the artist looking out. Jacob Jordaens painted himself with his family in about 1615.
still-life-with-cheeses-almonds-and-pretzels

Big wheels of cheese, a pile of almonds and a pretzel sit on a table, and in the shiny pewter jug you can see a tiny reflection of the artist. Clara Peeters painted it in about 1615, and she was one of the few women painting in the Netherlands.
the-garden-of-eden-with-the-fall-of-man
Adam and Eve stand under a tree in a garden full of animals, with a snake wrapped around the tree. Rubens painted the people and Jan Brueghel the Elder painted the animals and plants, in about 1615.
self-portrait-as-a-lute-player
A woman in a rich golden dress looks out from the picture, holding a lute, and she looks up as if she is thinking about a tune. Artemisia Gentileschi painted herself in about 1616.
self-portrait-as-saint-catherine-of-alexandria
A woman with dark hair rests her arm on the wheel with spikes, looking out at us. Artemisia Gentileschi painted herself as Saint Catherine in about 1616.
the-banquet-of-the-officers-of-the-st-george-militia-co

A table full of officers in sashes and ruffs drinks and chats, with a flag and food, in a very lively group. Frans Hals painted it in 1616, and it was one of the first paintings where a group of friends look relaxed.
christ-before-the-high-priest
Christ stands in a dark room lit by a single candle in front of a high priest, who tears his robe. Gerard van Honthorst painted it in about 1617, and the candle's glow is the star.
entry-of-christ-into-jerusalem
Christ rides a donkey into the city, with crowds laying palm branches and cloaks on the road. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1617, when he was about 18 years old.
the-lunch

Three men sit around a plain table with bread, a pomegranate and a jug, and look as if they're about to start eating. Diego Velázquez painted it in about 1617, when he was just a teenager, and the faces are as real as living people.
christ-in-the-house-of-martha-and-mary-velazquez

A young kitchen maid, with a mortar and eggs and fish, looks angry while she works, and through a window we see Christ talking with two women. Diego Velázquez painted it in 1618, at age 19, and the kitchen is the real subject.
et-in-arcadia-ego

Two shepherds stop in front of a skull sitting on a stone block marked with the words Et in Arcadia ego, which means 'Even in Arcadia, I exist.' Guercino painted it in about 1618, and it is a reminder that death is there even in the happiest places.
head-of-medusa
The snaky head of Medusa lies on the ground, with the snakes writhing and crawling, and some becoming scorpions and toads. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1618.
old-woman-cooking-eggs

An old woman pokes two eggs in a pan on a small stove while a boy looks at her, holding a melon and a bottle. Diego Velázquez painted it in 1618, and he was only 19, and the kitchen things are painted in a wonderfully shiny way.
the-battle-of-the-amazons
Warrior women on horses fight Greek soldiers on a wooden bridge in a whirl of swords, horses and bodies. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1618.
the-brazen-serpent
People bitten by snakes reach toward a bronze serpent on a pole, which heals them, in a crowded picture. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1618.
the-rape-of-the-daughters-of-leucippus

Two heroic twin brothers carry off two daughters of a king on their horses, with the women struggling in the arms of the men, in a rush of motion. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1618, and the story is from Greek myth.
three-musicians
Three young musicians play the guitar and violin and sing at a table, with a jug of wine. Diego Velázquez painted it in about 1618, when he was just starting out.
adoration-of-the-magi-velazquez
The three kings bring gifts to the baby Jesus in a close, dark room, with Mary holding him. Diego Velázquez painted it in 1619, when he was 20, and he used his own family as models.
the-raising-of-lazarus
Christ calls Lazarus out of his tomb, and Lazarus is helped out in his burial cloth while onlookers are astonished. Guercino painted it in 1619.
adoration-of-the-child-honthorst
Mary, Joseph and shepherds gaze at the baby Jesus, who glows brightly, lighting up their faces in the dark. Gerard van Honthorst painted it in about 1620.
cleopatra
The Egyptian queen Cleopatra lies on a bed, about to end her life, in a solemn, quiet scene. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1620.
conversion-of-the-magdalene

A woman in a rich yellow dress turns away from a mirror and raises her hand, as her sister speaks to her. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1620, and the story is about Mary Magdalene giving up her old life.
drunken-silenus
A fat, tipsy old man, a friend of the wine god Bacchus, is held up by satyrs while holding a cup, with grapes and a flushed face. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1620.
jael-and-sisera
A woman holds a mallet and a tent peg over a sleeping soldier, to save her people. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1620, from a Bible story.
judith-beheading-holofernes-gentilesch

Two women work together to cut off the head of an enemy general in a dark tent, with blood in the sheets. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in about 1620, and this second version is bigger and more dramatic than her first.
massacre-of-the-innocents-poussin

A mother tries to save her child in a terrible scene, as soldiers fight the mothers in a courtyard. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1625, and the mother's scream is one of the most famous faces in painting.
peace-urges-the-churches-to-tolerance
Peace, a woman in white, stands among figures representing churches and urges them to get along. An unknown painter made this allegory in the 1600s, when Europe was torn by religious wars.
saint-matthew-and-the-angel
A saint writes his Gospel while a boyish angel, standing behind him, guides his hand and counts on his fingers. Guido Reni painted it in about 1620.
the-crown-of-thorns
Christ, tied up, bows his head while soldiers press a crown of thorns onto it. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1620, and the faces are sharp and emotional.
the-waterseller-of-seville

An old man hands a glass of water to a boy, beside a large clay jar, with a fig dropping into the glass. Diego Velázquez painted it in about 1620, and the water drops on the jar are so real that you can almost feel the cool.
the-fall-of-the-damned
A swirling mass of bodies tumbles down into a fiery pit, in a giant picture of Judgment Day. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1621.
portrait-of-a-couple-probably-isaac-massa-and-beatrix-v

A young couple sit in a garden, and she rests her hand on his shoulder, as they smile at us. Frans Hals painted it in about 1622, and it is one of the first portraits of a happy, relaxed married couple.
portrait-of-don-luis-de-gongora
An old man in black, with a laurel wreath on his head, looks off to the side with a stern face. This portrait of the great Spanish poet Luis de Góngora was painted by Velázquez in 1622.
portrait-of-susanna-lunden
A woman in a big black hat looks out with a warm, steady gaze. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1622, and it is known as Le Chapeau de Paille, the straw hat, because of a mistaken name.
susanna-and-the-elders-gentilesch
Susanna sits in a garden as two men spy on her and whisper to her. Artemisia Gentileschi painted it in 1622.
danae-gentilesch-3
A maid holds out a cloth to catch gold coins falling, as Danaë reclines on a bed, with the golden shower. Orazio Gentileschi painted it in about 1623, and the glossy fabrics are painted wonderfully.
jester-with-lute
A man in a big hat and a ruffled coat strums a lute, laughing, with his mouth open. Frans Hals painted it in about 1624 in a bold, loose style.
laughing-cavalier

A young man in a black hat and richly embroidered sleeves looks out with a sly, half-smile and his arm on his hip. Frans Hals painted it in 1624, and the name Laughing Cavalier was given much later, though he is only slightly smiling.
the-stoning-of-saint-stephen
Men throw stones at Saint Stephen, who kneels with his eyes turned toward heaven. Rembrandt painted it in 1625 when he was only 18 or 19, and the young Saul, who is watching, is a self-portrait.
saint-martin-and-the-beggar-dyck
A knight on a white horse cuts his cloak in half with his sword to share it with a half-naked beggar. Anthony van Dyck painted it in about 1621 for a church in Belgium.
smiling-girl-a-courtesan-holding-an-obscene-image

A woman in a feathered hat laughs and holds up a picture, and the candlelight makes her face glow. Gerard van Honthorst painted it in 1625, in a style that makes the viewer part of the joke. This picture is meant for adults.
the-penitent-magdalen
A woman sits at a table in the dark with a candle, a mirror and a skull, thinking quietly. Georges de La Tour painted it in about 1625, and the soft candlelight makes it feel calm and still.
the-procuress-honthorst
A man and a woman at a table in a dark inn are lit by a candle, with an old woman on one side. Gerard van Honthorst painted it in 1625, and it is a picture for adults.
the-victory-of-joshua-over-the-amorites
Joshua's army chases the enemy under a dramatic sky, with a storm of hail and a shining sun and moon. Nicolas Poussin painted it in about 1625, and the story is from the Bible.
willem-van-heythuysen-posing-with-a-sword
A young man in a black outfit sits in a chair, leaning over the back, with a sword resting on his knee. Frans Hals painted it in about 1625, and the pose is relaxed and confident.
balaam-and-the-ass
A prophet raises his stick to hit his donkey, which has stopped because it sees an angel with a sword that he cannot see. Rembrandt painted it in 1626 when he was about 20.
drunken-silenus-ribera
A plump, red-faced old man lies on the ground drunk, with satyrs and a donkey around him. Jusepe de Ribera painted it in 1626.
gipsy-girl
A smiling young woman with loose hair and a dark dress looks out with a bold, laughing glance. Frans Hals painted it in about 1626, and it is a lively, quick sketch of a person.
crucifixion-of-christ
Christ hangs on a cross against a dark background, with the body painted as if it were a statue, lit by a single light. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1627 for monks to pray in front of.
rape-of-the-sabine-women
Roman soldiers carry off women from a neighboring city, in a crowded, twisting scene in a Roman square. Pietro da Cortona painted it in about 1627, and it tells a legend from Rome's early history.
lot-and-his-daughters-gentilesch
A man sits holding a glass while two women stand with him in a stage-like room, with the fire of a burning city in the distance. Orazio Gentileschi painted it in about 1628.
portrait-of-a-young-man-with-a-skull
A young man in a big hat holds a skull and looks at us, a reminder that life is short. Frans Hals painted it in about 1628.
saint-serapion
A monk in a white robe hangs from his wrists, dead, with his head slumped, in a quiet, stark picture. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1628, and the folds of the white cloak are unforgettable.
the-fall-of-man
Adam and Eve stand under a tree in a garden as Eve picks the fruit, with a parrot and a snake in the tree. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in about 1628 as a copy of Titian's painting.
the-triumph-of-bacchus
The god Bacchus crowns a kneeling drinker with ivy, as other men grin, drink and lift cups. Diego Velázquez painted it in 1628, and the men are painted as real Spanish peasants, not as gods.
a-militiaman-holding-a-berkemeyer-known-as-the-merry-dr
A man in a big hat raises a glass of wine with a big grin, looking right at us. Frans Hals painted it in about 1629, and it is known as the Merry Drinker.
apparition-of-the-apostle-peter-to-saint-peter-nolasco
Saint Peter, a vision, appears to a sleeping monk, with a cross, in a dark room. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in 1629.
coronation-of-saint-rosalia
A young woman kneels as an angel crowns her with roses, in a soft glow. Anthony van Dyck painted it in 1629 in Palermo, Sicily, where he painted several pictures of the city's saint.
